outcome: Prevalence of placental abnormalities (placenta accreta spectrum disorder, placenta previa)
Need for any intervention for placental separation during the third phase of delivery
cohort: The study included all women who gave birth in a single tertiary care center from February 2011 to January 2019 after undergoing myomectomy.
finding: Subsequent pregnancy following surgical myomectomy was not found to be associated with a higher prevalence of placental abnormality, and different modes of myomectomy did not necessitate further intervention for complications associated with abnormal placentation.
mod_finding: The vaginal delivery rate was significantly higher in the hysteroscopy group compared to the laparoscopy or laparotomy groups, which also had a significantly lower need for manual lysis of the placenta and further interventions for blood loss control.
